newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia eases bourse investment rules.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia eases bourse investment rules.

text.p: Tunisia has published laws allowing foreigners to buy up to 49 percent of companies listed on the Tunis exchange without prior authorisation and providing legal backing for development of the equities market.
One law, published in the official gazette received on Monday, raises to 49 percent from 10 percent the maximum stake a foreigner can buy without Central Bank authorisation.
A second law approves stock exchange easing of listing conditions, establishes a market garantee fund and improves transparency in dealings.
Under the new rules, firms no longer need a minimum capital of one million dinars ($925,000) to be listed on the first market, or 500,000 dinars for the secondary market.

Instead, they are required to sell through public offers a minimum 20 percent stake of their capital to at least 500 shareholders to be listed on the first market, and at least a 10 percent stake to at least 300 shareholders to be listed on the secondary market.
The garantee fund would be financed by brokers' contributions. ($=1.08 dinar) Tunis newsroom, 2161-787538
